question: What is the primary goal of quality care in reproductive health?

options.A: Increasing the speed of administrative discharge
options.C: Ensuring safe, effective, and respectful services
options.D: Reducing the total number of hospital admissions

explanation: Quality reproductive healthcare focuses on safety, effectiveness, and respecting client dignity to reduce preventable harm. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why does poor quality of care directly threaten maternal health outcomes?

options.A: It lengthens the duration of routine nursing shifts
options.B: It discourages clients from seeking timely skilled assistance
options.C: It automatically lowers the national budget for health
options.D: It increases the cost of medical equipment importation

explanation: When clients experience poor or disrespectful care, they delay seeking help, which worsens maternal mortality rates. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the main function of clinical governance in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Managing facility payroll and staff welfare packages
options.B: Controlling the procurement of pharmaceutical supplies
options.C: Holding organizations accountable for continuous quality improvement
options.D: Enforcing disciplinary actions for every clinical mistake

explanation: Clinical governance ensures institutions maintain accountability for high standards and safe patient care. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h2)

question: How does a blame-free culture support better patient safety outcomes?

options.A: It shifts legal responsibility entirely onto the patient
options.B: It stops nurses from ever making clinical mistakes again
options.C: It encourages staff to report errors openly for learning
options.D: It removes the need for any written hospital policies

explanation: Open reporting allows teams to analyze system failures without fear, preventing the same mistakes from happening twice. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of using clinical guidelines in a nursing unit?

options.A: To limit the clinical autonomy of junior nurses
options.B: To replace the need for physical nursing assessments
options.C: To eliminate guesswork and standardize patient interventions
options.D: To increase the paperwork required for each admission

explanation: Guidelines provide clear, evidence-based steps so care remains consistent and reliable across different shifts. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h3)

question: A nurse follows a national protocol to manage postpartum hemorrhage. What is the direct benefit of this action?

options.A: Complete elimination of all post-delivery complications
options.B: Reduction in the total number of hospital beds needed
options.C: Ensuring the patient receives proven, evidence-based care
options.D: Guaranteed promotion to a senior administrative position

explanation: National protocols incorporate best practices to maximize positive outcomes for acute conditions like hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the first step in conducting a clinical audit?

options.A: Selecting an explicit standard of care to measure
options.B: Purchasing new medical equipment for the ward
options.C: Discharging all stable patients from the unit
options.D: Punishing staff members who failed to meet targets

explanation: An audit always begins by defining the benchmark or standard against which current clinical practice will be measured. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why must a clinical audit be followed by a re-audit phase?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory legal requirements for annual licensing
options.B: To increase the cost of hospital service delivery
options.C: To find new staff members to blame for past errors
options.D: To check if implemented changes actually improved patient care

explanation: Re-auditing closes the quality loop by verifying whether the interventions successfully bridged the identified care gap. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the main objective of conducting a Root Cause Analysis after an adverse event?

options.A: To determine which individual worker should lose their license
options.B: To prepare a legal defense against patient lawsuits
options.C: To calculate the financial loss incurred by the hospital
options.D: To identify the underlying systemic failures that allowed the error

explanation: RCA looks beyond human error to uncover workflow, equipment, or communication flaws within the system. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why do punitive reporting systems often fail to improve patient safety?

options.A: They make clinical guidelines too long for nurses to read
options.B: They drive mistakes underground and discourage staff from reporting
options.C: They remove all legal protections from the healthcare facility
options.D: They cost the hospital too much money in administrative fees

explanation: When staff fear punishment, they hide near-misses and errors, preventing the facility from learning and fixing flaws. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h5)

question: How do surgical checklists primarily improve patient safety in the operating theatre?

options.A: By reducing the total duration of the surgical procedure
options.B: By replacing the need for an anesthetist during surgery
options.C: By acting as cognitive prompts to prevent memory lapses
options.D: By automatically sterilizing surgical instruments before use

explanation: Checklists ensure vital safety steps are explicitly verified, preventing human memory failure during busy procedures. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is a major communication benefit of using safety checklists in maternal care?

options.A: They allow senior surgeons to work without talking to nurses
options.B: They encourage all multidisciplinary team members to speak up
options.C: They transfer all clinical accountability to the patient
options.D: They eliminate the need to document care in the patient file

explanation: Checklists create a structured pause where every team member verifies safety steps, breaking down rigid hierarchies. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of utilizing patient satisfaction surveys in a hospital?

options.A: To determine the monthly salary of nursing personnel
options.B: To evaluate the clinical diagnostic skills of the medical director
options.C: To comply with pharmaceutical supply chain regulations
options.D: To capture the client's lived experience of care delivery

explanation: Satisfaction surveys give patients a voice to share how they perceived the quality and attitude of care received. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h7)

question: Which issue is most commonly uncovered through patient feedback in maternity wards?

options.A: Inadequate structural design of hospital laboratory equipment
options.C: Errors in calculating hospital corporate financial taxes
options.D: Unfriendly staff attitudes and poor communication

explanation: Patients frequently report interpersonal dynamics, communication gaps, and attitude issues that internal clinical audits might miss. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h7)

question: What distinguishes Continuous Quality Improvement from traditional quality assurance?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any nursing documentation
options.B: Viewing quality as an ongoing journey rather than a fixed end-point
options.C: Focusing exclusively on financial profit margins rather than health
options.D: Restricting quality control decisions to federal ministers

explanation: CQI treats quality improvement as a continuous, daily process of incremental testing and adaptation. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h8)

question: Why is local team empowerment essential for successful CQI implementation in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: It removes the need for any hospital management oversight
options.B: Staff closest to daily operations best understand where workflows fail
options.C: It guarantees external international funding for the facility
options.D: It ensures that nurses never have to work night shifts again

explanation: Empowering frontline nurses allows them to identify practical solutions tailored to their specific resource realities. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h8)
